gloss: early on; promptly; right away; without delay

definitions.explanation: Doing something soon after a certain point in time, without delay or lingering. Often implies leaving or finishing sooner than might be expected.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}は{早々|そうそう}に{切|き}り{上|あ}げられた。
examples.english: The meeting was wrapped up promptly.

examples.japanese: {新年|しんねん}{早々|そうそう}に{風邪|かぜ}を{引|ひ}いてしまい、{出|で}だしが{悪|わる}かった。
examples.english: I caught a cold right at the start of the new year, so I got off to a bad start.

notes:
Often follows a time expression or event to mean "right at the beginning of" or "soon after": {新年|しんねん}{早々|そうそう} (right at the start of the new year), {到着|とうちゃく}{早々|そうそう} (right after arriving). In this suffix-like usage, に is often omitted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新年|しんねん}{早々|そうそう}: right at the start of the new year
- {到着|とうちゃく}{早々|そうそう}: right after arriving
- {開店|かいてん}{早々|そうそう}: right after opening
- {早々|そうそう}に{引|ひ}き{上|あ}げる: to withdraw early
- {早々|そうそう}に{切|き}り{上|あ}げる: to wrap up early

USAGE:
As a standalone adverb ({早々|そうそう}に), it means "promptly, without lingering." As a suffix attached to nouns (X{早々|そうそう}), it means "right at the start of X" or "soon after X." Note the different reading: {早々|はやばや}と means "hastily" with a nuance of doing something sooner than originally planned.
